issues.description: Collapsing 'working' and 'walking' states changes the DFS data model without documenting the merged invariant.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag that the two labels previously encoded distinct DFS phases (children-queued vs currently-descending) and that push()'s cycle-detection reads this state. The merge may be correct, but no loop invariant or state-machine spec is written down. State explicitly that a node is 'walking' iff its children have been pushed but not yet drained, and verify push() still behaves correctly.

issues.description: Yield-false early-return path no longer marks node sorted, coupling correctness to the deferred clear.
issues.detail: Previously s.state[k] = sorted ran unconditionally after pop; now it only runs on yield=true. The deferred clear papers over this, but the postcondition of the loop body changed silently. Document that partial iteration discards all progress and that early-return relies on the defer wiping state, or the next maintainer will break it.

issues.description: Sorter reuse contract and cleanup lifetime change is undocumented.
issues.detail: Moving clear() into a defer changes when Sorter state is released (on iterator completion rather than next Sort entry) and establishes a new reuse contract. The reentrant-panic case also leaves the invariant ambiguous. Add a short spec comment on the Sorter type stating preconditions, postconditions, and reuse semantics so the contract is not asserted only in prose.

issues.description: No regression test asserts the reuse invariant the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: The PR description says it fixes state reuse, non-zero stack elements, and cleanup on completion, but no test in the diff exercises this. Add a test calling Sort twice on the same Sorter with different graphs, asserting results and that len(s.stack)==0 and len(s.state)==0 after iteration. Without it, correctness is asserted only in prose.

issues.description: Updated comment has typos ('visisted', 'if its') in load-bearing documentation.
issues.detail: All three reviewers note the new comment reads 'whether this node has been visisted and if its the first or second visit'. Since this comment is now the de-facto specification of the state machine, the typos invite readers to skim past it. Fix to 'visited' and 'it's' and tighten the prose.

issues.description: clear(s.stack) followed by reslicing to zero length needs intent stated.
issues.detail: clear() zeroes every backing-array element, then s.stack = s.stack[:0] drops the length. If the stack holds pointer-bearing values this is correct GC hygiene; if value types, it is wasted work. Add a one-line comment stating the intent so a future reader does not 'optimize' it away or duplicate the ceremony.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges: collapsing 'working' and 'walking' into one state and moving cleanup into a defer is the right direction, but the PR is presented as a routine cleanup when it is actually a data-model and contract change. The merged state machine, the new Sorter reuse contract, and the changed postcondition on yield-false early-return are all undocumented, and no regression test exercises the reuse invariant the PR claims to fix. Conditionally acceptable: require a short spec comment on Sorter stating the state machine, preconditions, and postconditions; fix the comment typos; and add a reuse regression test before merge.
